goal.objective:
Make audits folder/project-scoped to the current cwd project: the primary audit target is the folder where pi was opened; external code (parent repo, sibling projects, libraries outside cwd) may be READ to diagnose a failure affecting the current project and may be reported as a finding only when it blocks or breaks the current project, but typo/nit fixes in unrelated projects are out of scope and never auto-queued.

Boundaries: no changes to unrelated sibling projects for cosmetic issues; external library findings are DECIDE or FIX only when they affect current project's correctness. Hellhunter example: opening pi in web/games/wip/hellhunter audits hellhunter, not the entire dracon-platform.

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: lets audit the entire entire game and fix what we can, we would also need a ton of auto generated loot taht gets better as we have better loot and enemies that get better as we have better loot. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

(3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". tasks.verificationContract: Add behavioral regressions for recovery-resume, session handoff, and pending-list records dated in the future; run the focused lifecycle/recovery tests and npm run check.

subtasks.title: Verify all freshness validators and their shared semantics
Reject future timestamps without weakening stale/identity fences
Add tests covering all affected sidecar types
Check the finding with the resulting commit

tasks.title: Make tracked transcript tails discoverable
tasks.verificationContract: Add a regression for a matching transcript beyond the current 25-file window; preserve bounded main-thread I/O or document a safer index/lookup; run agents-panel and display tests plus npm run check.

subtasks.title: Confirm the 25-file cap is the actual failure mode
Implement a bounded, identity-safe lookup that does not silently hide tracked children
Add a regression for the older matching transcript
Check the finding with the resulting commit

tasks.title: Route audit fan-out through the selected state root
tasks.verificationContract: Add a sessionDir regression proving list-audit fan-out reads the selected GLLA state root and queues findings; run list-audit, state-root, and release/type checks.

subtasks.title: Trace the runtime root registration and detached fan-out boundary
Use the admitted state-root resolver without weakening generation fences
Add a hermetic sessionDir fan-out test
Check the finding with the resulting commit

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

tasks.title: Reconcile package-store-facing installation docs
tasks.verificationContract: Resolve the docs/INDEX.md versus INSTALL.md symlink-setup mismatch, review README.md for current shipped behavior, and prove README/INSTALL/docs are included in npm pack output; run npm run check.

subtasks.title: Choose source-install wording that matches the supported commands

Run a package dry-run and document release-version/Unreleased status
Check the finding with the resulting commit

tasks.title: Run release gate and final audit review
tasks.verificationContract: Run npm run release:check, inspect all new findings and commits, and obtain a final read-only reviewer report; every new FIX is checked with a real commit and no DECIDE remains unraised.

subtasks.title: Run focused regressions and the full release contract
Re-audit changed boundaries and release/package documentation
Record environment-only failures separately if the gate is blocked
Prepare the six-label completion evidence

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

auditHistory.report:
## Audit

The audit contract is satisfied: four new FIX findings are checked, their commits exist, and no DECIDE findings remain. The release gate also passed.

However, the package-store requirement is not complete. The repository README contains new release guidance, but the published npm/Pi package is still `0.36.1` and does not contain that marker:

```text
--- source marker ---
40:for published versions. The npm/Pi package listing displays this README from
--- registry marker ---
--- registry metadata ---
version = '0.36.1'
dist-tags.latest = '0.36.1'
time.modified = '2026-08-31T00:49:31.797Z'
```

The completion summary itself says publishing is still the next step. Thus the user-facing store README remains stale.

<evidence>
Item: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).
Output:
- [x] FIX: MEDIUM: recovery-resume, session-handoff, and pending-list sidecars accept future-dated timestamps because freshness checks only require `Date.now() - at < window` (`extensions/goal-recovery.ts:63`; `extensions/loops/goal-session.ts:796,860,915`) — a future marker can be consumed as fresh and trigger an unexpected resume or replay. Require a non-negative age and add regressions for every sidecar validator. — fixed in 265dafa6 (shared non-negative-age gate + 3 regression tests)

Output:
- [x] FIX: MEDIUM: recovery-resume, session-handoff, and pending-list sidecars accept future-dated timestamps because freshness checks only require `Date.now() - at < window` (`extensions/goal-recovery.ts:63`; `extensions/loops/goal-session.ts:796,860,915`) — a future marker can be consumed as fresh and trigger an unexpected resume or replay. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix

- Antigravity poll-only inferred 250→1000ms (scripts/durable-wait.mjs)

## Audit report — pi-goal-list-loop-audit v0.38.18 trilogy

**Verdict: work is a partial fix with two tracks re-scoped away from the contract.**

What was checked:
- `tests/mechanical-pipeline.test.ts` (7 tests), `tests/never-streamed-standdown.test.ts` (4), `tests/terminal-completion-notice.test.ts` (2) read in full; targeted `bun test` re-run (9 pass); `tsc --noEmit` clean; `CHANGELOG.md`, `audit/COMPLETION-LIFECYCLE-TRILOGY-2026-09-04.md`, `docs/INDEX.md`/`audit/INDEX.md`, `git tag`, `npm view` inspected.
- Track 1 is real: narrow `cmd 2>&1 | tail/head/grep` pipeline parsed and run shell-free with head-exit semantics; `tee`/redirect/chain refused with no side effects. This matches objective Track 1 ("checker handling pipeline syntax").
- Track 2 does NOT satisfy the objective/contract. Objective demands: "after the user answers ask_user_question, no continuation turn starts — root-cause the dispatch stall, not the aborter." The shipped fix does the opposite: it parks never-streamed turns on first abort (`zombie_auto_retry_refused_never_streamed`, no retry) and rewords the rearm milestone. The regression file contains zero references to `ask_user_question` and no answered-question→continuation-turn behavioral test. Forensics in the audit doc even re-blames the field case to "never streamed, not dispatch."
- Track 3 does NOT satisfy the contract literal. Contract demands "a closed goal clears the waiting-verdict state." The shipped fix sends a fire-once `followUp` `✓ done` notice (`sendTerminalCompletionNotice`) but never clears the `awaiting-verdict` display phase (`goal-loop-display.ts` still returns `awaiting-verdict` for `phase complete` / `pendingCompletion running`). The test pins `pi.sent` growth + source wiring, not state cleared on close.
- Release/docs/publish trail exists (tag `v0.38.18`, `npm view = 0.38.18`, CHANGELOG + audit doc + INDEX entries), but full `release:check` (1912 pass claim) was not reproduced here — only targeted files + `tsc`. No recursion violation found (pipeline tests use string parsing + `node --version | tail`, never spawn the suite runner).
- Visual audit: no fresh screenshots were supplied in this audit session; `audit/COMPLETION-LIFECYCLE-TRILOGY-2026-09-04.md` references `Screenshot_20260904_152601/153208/153934.png` but those files are not in the repo listing. Critique versus objective: cannot visually confirm the endless-td/neonbreak/junk-runner symptoms or their resolution — verdict rests on code/tests alone. Verbatim critique for the visual contract item: "Visual evidence unavailable — no image attachments in audit context; screenshot filenames cited in audit doc but not present for fresh inspection, so UI before/after cannot be critiqued."
